quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jim Schmidt: Q3 product and royalty revenue $197.1 million, up 37.5% sequentially from $143.4 million and 78.5% from $110.4 million a year earlier; advanced products revenue (including royalties) up 47.5% sequentially to $138.9 million and Brick products up 18.4% to $58.3 million; royalty revenue up 119.1% sequentially to $66.6 million, a fraction of it non-recurring initial royalty payments from the new licensee; advanced products were 70.4% of revenue; shipments to stocking distributors up 24.8% sequentially; exports about 36.1% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $197.1 million, up 37.5% sequentially and 78.5% year-over-year

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jim Schmidt: Q3 gross margin 68.3%, up 1,030 basis points sequentially and 1,080 basis points year-over-year on higher royalty revenue and better product margins (volume, efficiency, mix); operating expense up 29.6% to $62.5 million, with legal expense (largely contingent on royalty revenue) up about $11.1 million to $16.1 million and expected to average about 20% of royalty revenue near term; net income $63.3 million, $1.33 per diluted share; operating cash flow $69.7 million, capex $16.1 million, cash $513.1 million; construction in progress, mainly manufacturing equipment, about $26.4 million with about $48.6 million left to spend; operating ratios approaching the long-term financial model.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 68.3%; net income $63.3 million; cash $513.1 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jim Schmidt, Q4 outlook (no formal guidance, CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli citing licensing uncertainty): with incremental capacity Vicor expects a 10% increase in Q4 product revenue (CEO: a low double-digit increase), including another double-digit sequential increase in advanced products, and at least $43 million of royalty revenue assuming no new license agreements close in the quarter (CEO: 'a very conservative number'); CEO: licensing income is now expected to reach levels next year and the year after beyond what he forecast a year ago, with lumpiness.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 product revenue up 10%; royalty revenue at least $43 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jim Schmidt and VP Phil Davies: Q3 book-to-bill above one and one-year backlog up 7% sequentially to $406 million (CEO: closer to $400 million as of the day before the call); $100 million of bookings in the first two weeks of Q4, including a large order for second-generation VPD modules from the lead customer; leading ATE customers for ASIC and memory test systems now represent over $100 million in annual revenue and capacity reservations are being discussed; CEO: a major customer sees demand doubling every year for the next several years, and the CEO of another major (non-AI) customer wants to reserve capacity over the next few years.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $406 million, up 7%; $100 million of bookings in the first two weeks of Q4

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli on capacity: Vicor is getting closer to full utilization of ChiP Fab-1 and has near-term capacity limits tied to specific process steps; Fab-2 in Merrimack (within an existing building, including a 330,000 sq ft building) is likely to get initial equipment in Q2 2027 for the most constrained process steps; land for Fab-3 closed about a week before the call but no building is planned for now; Fab-2 and Fab-3 support a conservative nearly 5x capacity increase relative to Fab-1, funded without raising capital; capital investment figures may come on the next call.
quarterly_data.figure: initial Fab-2 equipment in Q2 2027; nearly 5x capacity

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli and VP Phil Davies on licensing: Vicor granted its first VPD license to a leading AI OEM at stage-two unit royalty rates, and the same licensee placed another significant license PO early in Q4; two hyperscalers inquired about all-inclusive licenses, quoted at stage two and stage three before the ITC instituted its VPD infringement investigation; Vicor has asked the ITC for a limited exclusion order on unlicensed computing systems; royalty rates escalate by stage (about 5% per month during the roughly 10 months of stage three before the hearing), licensees have most-favored-licensee terms, and management now treats royalty revenue as recurring.
quarterly_data.figure: about 5% per month royalty escalation in stage three

quarterly_data.signal: VP Phil Davies and CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli on technology: at Open Compute, OEMs and hyperscalers saw second-generation VPD demos; Vicor's ALL-FPA enables a 10%-15% reduction in AI processor power loss with over 40 times the current gain of IVRs and three times the current density of VRs, and demo systems are set up in its Silicon Valley applications lab; second-generation VPD demonstration vehicles reached 3 amps per square millimeter, with 5 to 6 amps per square millimeter not far off; the CEO puts the extra power dissipation of an IVR stage at upwards of 10% and close to 15%, and says a hyperscaler told Vicor it would be the only solution for feeding IVRs at 1.8 volt; adoption of second-generation VPD beyond the lead customer is still early (Davies).
quarterly_data.figure: 10%-15% lower AI processor power loss; 3 amps per square millimeter
